proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage sequence. Stage 1: Oxidation of alcohol to aldehyde using organic peroxide at 40°C. Critical constraint: Amine cannot contact peroxide. Therefore, Amine is added via Stream B only after Stage 1 residence time is complete. Stage 2: Condensation of aldehyde with amine at 80°C. No light source required. BPR not required as temperatures are below solvent boiling points (assuming standard organic solvents like DCM/DCM or EtOAc, bp > 40-80°C with margin, or if high bp solvent used). Calculations suggest mass transfer limitation in Stage 1, so efficient mixing at the inlet of Stage 1 is crucial.

reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Stage 1 is 40°C per Chemistry Plan. Stage 2 is 80°C. The hardware parameters listed are for Stage 1. Stage 2 would require a second heating zone.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation says BPR not required. case.title: Two-stage sequence with incompatible feeds
case.protocol: Stage 1 oxidizes an alcohol with an organic peroxide at 40 C for 20 min. The resulting aldehyde must then be mixed with an amine, but direct contact of the amine with the peroxide feed is prohibited. Stage 2 proceeds at 80 C for 45 min. Design a continuous sequence with explicit delayed addition and residence time for each stage.
